40B India-First Coding Model: Data Plan

By Avnish Midha

Goal: a Gemma-4-class 40B model, optimized in this order: coding, agentic work, then Indic languages, while defaulting to Indian context for law, governance, commerce, education, culture and daily life.

40B dense 128K-256K context coding-first agentic India-first

Core decision: train on ~20T high-quality tokens. Allocate more budget to code than a general model, but keep enough Indian and Indic data to change the model’s defaults, not just its translation ability.

Pre-training data

BucketTarget shareCollectWhy

Include Indian API ecosystems: UPI, GST, ONDC, DigiLocker, Aadhaar sandbox docs where permitted.

STEM12%Textbooks, papers, proofs, problem sets, worked solutions, symbolic dataSupports coding, reasoning and engineering tasks.

Post-training and RL/alignment

  • SFT: 20M-40M high-quality examples: coding tasks with tests, repo Q&A, tool-use conversations, long-context document QA, Indian legal/finance/government assistance, Indic and code-mixed chat.
  • Coding RL: execution feedback from unit tests, compilers, linters and hidden tests. Reward passing tests, minimal patches, secure code and clear explanations.
  • Agentic RL: tool-use success, valid JSON, fewer unnecessary calls, correct clarification, state tracking, and final answers grounded in observations.
  • India-first preference data: Indian raters and experts reward answers that know jurisdiction, date, state, rupees, Indian exams, Indian addresses, and local cultural assumptions.
  • Safety: multilingual red-teaming for caste, religion, gender, communal violence, self-harm, cyber abuse, financial fraud and legal/medical overclaiming.

Cleaning pipeline

  • All data: license filter, PII/secrets removal, malware/CSAM filters, boilerplate removal, language ID, exact + near dedup, source metadata, benchmark decontamination.
  • Code: remove forks/vendor/minified/generated files, scan secrets, keep repo structure, tests and docs, verify build/test signals when possible.
  • Indic: preserve native scripts; do not over-normalize nukta, virama, ZWJ/ZWNJ, matras or Urdu diacritics. Keep romanized Indic and code-mix as first-class data with tags.
  • Indian domain: keep date, state, ministry, court, version and jurisdiction. Separate current factual QA from historical/legal pretraining text.
  • Agent traces: keep only valid tool schemas, real observations, successful or instructive failures, no fake tool results, no leaked credentials.

Code extraction Extract at repository level: approved license → fork/mirror dedup → keep source, tests, docs, configs, notebooks, issues/PRs when allowed → drop minified, generated, vendored, binary and secret-bearing files. Convert repos into completion, fill-in-middle, bug-fix, test-repair, API-use and agentic edit traces, then decontaminate against HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench and internal evals.

Language selection

P0logic: guarantee state/UT-level anchor coverage, not just population ranking. Each state or major UT cluster gets at least one anchor language; sampling within P0 is weighted by speakers, digital volume, government/commerce use and product demand.

P0anchors: Indian English, Hinglish, Hindi, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Odia, Assamese, Manipuri/Meitei, Khasi/Garo, Mizo, Nagamese + Ao/Angami, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Konkani, Kashmiri/Urdu, Ladakhi/Bhoti, Nepali, Santali, Maithili.

P1/P2regional coverage: Awadhi, Bhojpuri, Braj, Bundeli, Magahi, Angika, Rajasthani/Marwari/Mewari, Haryanvi, Chhattisgarhi, Garhwali, Kumaoni, Dogri, Tulu, Kodava, Bodo, Kokborok, Gondi, Ho, Mundari, Kurukh, Bhili, Nicobarese and other consented tribal/border languages.

Full state/UT language coverage table is included in References.

Fertility and tokenizer

AreaFertility target
English≤1.35 tokens/word
Code≤1.15 tokens per lexical token; preserve whitespace/indentation efficiently
Math/scienceStable digit splitting, LaTeX/operator coverage; no equation fragmentation pathologies
P0 IndicAverage ≤1.8 tokens/word; no language >2.2
P1 IndicAverage ≤2.2; no language >2.8
Code-mix≤2.0-2.3

Tokenizer decision: custom SentencePiece unigram/BPE with byte fallback, preserved whitespace, split digits and 96k vocabulary plus 2k-4k reserved control/tool tokens. Gemma uses ~262k, but for this coding-first 40B model, 96k is the better tradeoff: lower embedding/inference cost, enough coverage for 22 scheduled languages, and explicit fertility targets for Indic scripts.

Final position

This is not a Hindi chatbot with code bolted on. It is a coding-first base model with agentic training and India-aware defaults. The differentiator is the combination of repo-level executable code, real tool traces, Indian institutional data with metadata, multilingual Indic coverage, and preference data judged by Indian users and experts.
